Welcome! I’m so glad you’re here, because together, we’re about to pull back the curtain on how the world really works—often in ways you’d never expect.
Have you ever wondered what happens when we start asking the questions nobody else dares to ask? Or what might emerge if we let economic thinking guide us through the hidden corners of everyday life?
That’s exactly the adventure Steven D. Levitt invites us on in his eye-opening book, SuperFreakonomics. He takes us on a journey that’s as surprising as it is fun—challenging everything we thought we knew about why people make the choices they do, and how society ticks.
Along the way, we’ll dig into stories that turn the ordinary upside down. Like, what could connect global cooling to human behavior? Why might a prostitute actually be more patriotic than a politician? And what on earth would motivate a suicide bomber to think about life insurance?
With each twist and turn, Levitt shines a light on the fascinating dance between incentives, trade-offs, and those unintended consequences we all too often overlook. We’ll explore bold experiments, quirky real-life tales, and plenty of unexpected logic that’ll have you seeing the world with entirely fresh eyes.
So, if you’re ready to question the obvious and dive deep into the surprising logic behind our everyday decisions, you’re in the right place. Let’s explore this wild, data-driven world of SuperFreakonomics together—and discover just how many secrets are hiding in plain sight.
